newsitem.title: UK: British couple jailed for central bank fraud plot.
newsitem.headline: British couple jailed for central bank fraud plot.

text.p: A British couple who tried to cash a 10 million pound ($17 million) cheque stolen from the Bank of England were each sentenced to three and a half years in prison on Friday.
Business consultant Peter Garnett and his accountant wife Linda almost got away with their audacious plan to defraud the 300-year-old central bank.

"The seriousness of this offence lies not only in the amount involved, but the fact that the cheque used was the first stolen from the Bank of England and forged," judge Kenneth Zucker told the couple at a court in southern England.

The couple were found out at the last minute because their own bank had grown suspicious of their lavish lifestyle, gained from other frauds, which included owning several homes, taking Caribbean holidays and running three cars -- a Rolls Royce, a Jaguar and a Mercedes.
It was only when the bank in Grantham, central England, phoned the central bank to find out whether the 9.7 million pound cheque was genuine that anyone realised it was missing.
It had been taken from a cheque book the Bank of England used to buy certificates of deposit and was signed with two "expertly-forged" signatures, the court heard.

Despite extensive inquiries, the bank never discovered who had stolen it. Peter Garnett claimed an Armenian businessman with gold teeth had handed it to him at King's Cross station in London as part of a property deal in Spain.
The prosecution dismissed this claim as "so ridiculous" it could not be true.

Linda Garnett also received a concurrent 18-month jail sentence for swindling the veterinary practice she worked for out of 73,000 pounds. The couple were found guilty late last month but were only sentenced on Friday.
